title: BARDING PROSE - the barding AC factors and weight doctrine
audit_comment: OA round thirty-five (capture pp. 98-99): the barding prose - the AC factors, the weights and the half-barding doctrine

banner.title: BARDING PROSE, printed capture pp. 98-99 - the OA barding prose round
banner.provenance: pinned from the 2018 print capture (the settling authority), with the compressed-print capture giving a second independent read of the section - the barding prose cross-checked paragraph-by-paragraph between the two passes (the intro on capture p. 98, the AC-factor list on capture p. 99 of the print pass); every printed number agrees - zero contested cells. The AC-factor list pins: leather or padded adds 1 factor to the AC and weighs 160#, metal scale adds 2 factors and weighs 250#, chain adds 3 factors and weighs 350#. The half-barding doctrine pins as consts and bools: half barding weighs half the amount of full barding (the divisor 2), increases the AC for frontal attacks only, and attacks from the rear do not gain the AC bonus; half barding is more frequently used than full barding, and half covers the head, neck and forequarters while full covers the entire body (the coverage split rides the comments). The materials paragraph pins: the most common material is quilted and padded cotton, the others in descending order are leather, leather scale, brigandine, metal scale and chain mail (the order rides the comment), and plate barding is never used - as a rule barding is only used on the mounts of important nobles, generals and shock troops (the mounts-only rule rides the comment). The warhorse must be able to carry the barding weight in addition to the rider and any equipment - and the movement-rate reduction cross-references the Table 55 grid already pinned in R646. The armor descriptions box stays open - the last Chapter 5 box
